1423	## Storage pre-flight double-count — postmortem (2026-07-25, commit `05e6605`)
1424	
1425	`lib/actions-migrate.ts` added the Docker image allowance into `items.totalBytes`, but
1426	`worker/migrate-real.ts` reads that value as `fileBytes` and adds the Docker allowance **itself**. A
1427	~12 GB move was therefore reported as needing **83.6 GB** and refused. The contract is now stated at
1428	the return site: `items.totalBytes` is **files only** (selected paths + the DB data-dir estimate);
1429	the worker owns the Docker + headroom arithmetic.
1430	
1431	**Customer impact:** the inflated figure led to a purchase of ~40 GB of disk that was not needed.
1432	Disk growth is deliberately one-way (no shrink path exists), so that spend is unrecoverable —
1433	recorded here because the money consequence, not the arithmetic, is why this must not recur.
1434	
1435	## Billing: subscription renewals have no card auto-charge (2026-07-25, finding)
1436	
1437	Renewals debit the **wallet only**. `worker/billing.ts` charges via `debitWallet`; on
1438	`InsufficientBalanceError` it falls through to grace and then suspends. There is **no saved-card path
1439	anywhere**: no `setup_future_usage`, no SetupIntent, no `off_session` `PaymentIntent`.
1440	`User.stripePaymentMethodId` exists in the schema but is **never written and never read** (only a
1441	mention in `app/api/account/export/route.ts`). `User.autoRechargeEnabled` /
1442	`autoRechargeThresholdCents` / `autoRechargeAmountCents` are settable through
1443	`lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts` — whose own comment concedes "the actual off-session Stripe charge is
1444	wired by the orchestrator" — but **nothing calls that action and nothing consumes those columns**.
1445	
1446	Consequence: a customer with a perfectly good card is suspended when their wallet empties. Agreed
1447	design — **wallet credit applied first, card auto-charged for the remainder** (consistent with
1448	`walletSplit`, which checkout already uses), dunning retries on days 1/3/5, suspension only after the
1449	card genuinely fails. Six dunning templates now exist on `emails.*` in `lib/mailer.ts`
1450	(`paymentReceipt`, `paymentFailed`, `paymentRetryFailed`, `paymentActionRequired`,
1451	`paymentFinalNotice`, `cardExpiringSoon`); the charging engine itself is **not built yet**.

# Nxeon — Server Migration Runbook

How to move Nxeon to a better dedicated server **without losing data**. Two parts move
independently: the **control plane** (Postgres + web + worker + nginx) and the **customer VMs**
(Proxmox guests). There are two strategies — pick based on how much downtime you can tolerate.

The golden rule: **never decommission the old server until the new one is verified serving.**
Everything below keeps the old server intact as a fallback the whole time.

---

## What state must move

| State | Where | How it moves |
|---|---|---|
| Databases (`nxeon`, `nxeon_staging`) | Postgres on host | `pg_dump` → `pg_restore` (the source of truth: users, servers, domains, wallets, invoices) |
| App code | `/opt/nxeon`, `/opt/nxeon-staging` | `git clone` from GitHub (already versioned) |
| Secrets | `/opt/nxeon/.env`, `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` | copied in the migration bundle (chmod 600) |
| Customer VMs | Proxmox ZFS `vmdata` | `vzdump` → `qmrestore`, **or** add new box as a node and migrate VM-by-VM |
| Templates 9000–9004 | Proxmox | `vzdump`/`qmrestore` or rebuild from `scripts/onboard-node.sh` |
| TLS certs | Let's Encrypt | **re-issued** on the new IP once DNS points there (don't copy) |
| nginx / systemd / firewall | `/etc/*` | regenerated by `configure-domains.sh` + `firewall.nft` (in repo) |

The **public IP changes** (new box = new IP). That ripples into: platform DNS (`revsports.ca`
A-records), customer domains pointed at the old IP, and every VPS's SSH endpoint
...
1:# Nxeon — Server Migration Runbook
12:## What state must move
32:## Strategy A — Graceful, VM-by-VM (recommended, minimal downtime)
57:## Strategy B — Full cutover (simpler, one maintenance window)
88:## Guaranteeing no data loss (do these every time)
101:## After migration

# Nxeon — Internal Product & Operations Manual

**Audience:** whoever is on the hook for this platform — building it, operating it, or answering a
customer whose server is down. It is written to be sufficient on its own: if you can read this and
reach a shell, you can run Nxeon.

**Rendered at** `/admin/docs` (staff only) from `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` on disk, via the in-house
renderer `lib/markdown.ts`. The viewer splits the document at every H2 into a searchable section
list, so **every H2 below is a navigation entry** — search for the thing you need rather than
scrolling.

**How this document is organised**

| Part | Contents |
|---|---|
| I — Orientation | What Nxeon is, architecture, request and job lifecycles, environments, flags, codebase map |
| II — Feature chapters | One chapter per feature: screen, workflow, code entry points, data model, failure modes, how an admin diagnoses it |
| III — Runbooks | The operational procedures, in the order you will need them |
| IV — Troubleshooting | Symptom → cause → fix tables, mined from real incidents |
| V — Reference | The Prisma data model, model by model |
| VI — Known gaps | What is **not** true yet. Read this before promising anything to a customer |
| VII — Change log | The historical dated entries, preserved |

**Conventions used throughout**

- Every `file:line` reference was read at the time of writing. Line numbers drift; the symbol name
  next to them is the durable part — grep for that if a line has moved.
- **Verified** means I read the code path or observed the live system. **Not true yet** means the
  code exists but does not do what the UI claims. Those two labels are load-bearing.
- Money is always integer cents. Times are UTC.

> **A warning about this codebase's dominant defect class.** The single most common bug here is not
> a crash — it is a value computed correctly and then discarded by its caller, or a setting saved and
> read by nothing, while the UI reports success. Two independent audits
> (`docs/AUDIT-24H.md`, `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md`) converged on that finding. When you read a feature
> chapter below, the *Failure modes* and *Not true yet* subsections are the parts that will save you.

---

## What Nxeon is

Nxeon is a Hostinger-style VPS hosting business running on **one OVH dedicated server** (KS-GAME,
i7-7700K, 64 GB RAM, 2×450 GB NVMe in a ZFS mirror plus a 4 TB HDD backup pool) under **Proxmox VE
9**. Customers sign up, pay, and get a real KVM virtual machine they have root on.

What it sells, in the order it makes money:

| Product | Model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| VPS plans | `Plan` → `Server` | 5 tiers, Nano $6.49 → Max $32.99/mo. Dedicated IPv4 included in the price |
| Game servers | `GamePlan` → `Server` | Same VMs, per-game sizing and pricing, 14 seeded tiers |
| Per-server extra disk | `Server.extraDiskGB` | One-way growth, billed over the term |
| Block-storage volumes | `Volume` | Separate Proxmox disks, per-GB pricing |
| Business email | `EmailPlan` → `EmailSubscription` → `Mailbox` | Mailboxes on the platform's own Mailcow |
| Domains | `Domain` | Registration and inbound transfer via name.com / Namecheap |
| SSL | `SslCertificate` | One-click Let's Encrypt onto the customer's own VM |

And the things that are not products but are why customers choose it: a **free lift-and-shift
migration** from their existing host, a **cPanel-style control panel**, an **in-browser terminal and
console**, **Claude Code pre-installed on every VPS**, and a **self-hosted white-label webmail**.

Two web surfaces share one Next.js app:

- **Customer portal** — `app/dashboard/**`, served on `https://nxeon.cloud`.
- **Admin ops portal** — `app/admin/**`, served only on the secret host
  `4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud`. On the customer host the `/admin` path returns 404 — the ops portal
  is hidden, not merely protected.

Plus a marketing site (`app/(marketing)/**`), a blog, 12 free SEO tool pages, and legal pages, all in
the same app.

The design system lives in `app/globals.css` plus `components/ui/primitives.tsx` and
`components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). There are no chart libraries and no UI
framework beyond Tailwind v4 — do not add either.

---

## Architecture map

Five moving parts. The web app never mutates Proxmox directly; it writes a `Job` row and the worker
does the work. That single rule is the backbone of the whole system.

```
                                  internet
                                      |
                          :80 / :443 / :8080 / :8443
                                      |
                     +----------------v-----------------+
                     |        nginx (host, :80/:443)    |
                     |  vhosts generated by             |
                     |  scripts/configure-domains.sh    |
                     +--+------+--------+---------+-----+
                        |      |        |         |
        nxeon.cloud     |      |        |         |   mail.nxeon.cloud
        4j3d...cloud    |      |        |         |   -> https://10.20.0.10
                        |      |        |         |
                 :3000  |  :8899        |  :8901  |            :3001 (staging)
                        |  console-ws   |  term-ws|
          +-------------v--+  +---------v--+  +---v---------+
          | nxeon-web      |  | console-   |  | nxeon-      |
          | Next.js 15     |  | proxy.mjs  |  | terminal    |
          | User=nxeon     |  | (noVNC     |  | (xterm PTY  |
          | npm start      |  |  relay)    |  |  websocket) |
          +---+--------+---+  +-----+------+  +------+------+
              |        |            |                |
   server     |        | read-only  |  websocket to  | ssh into
   actions    |        | status     |  Proxmox VNC   | the guest
              |        |            |                |
              |        +------------+----------------+
              |                     |
        writes Job rows             |
              |                     v
      +-------v----------+   +------------------------------+
      | PostgreSQL 17    |   |  Proxmox VE 9  (this host)   |
      |  db: nxeon       |   |  API token nxeon@pve!platform|
      |  db: nxeon_staging|  |                              |
      +-------^----------+   |  templates  9000-9009        |
              |              |  customer VMs 100+           |
       polls Job every 3s    |  mail VM  8000 (10.20.0.10)  |
              |              |  storage: vmdata (ZFS NVMe)  |
      +-------+----------+   |           vmdata-hdd         |
      | nxeon-worker     +-->|           backup (/tank)     |
      | tsx worker/      |   +------------------------------+
      | index.ts, ROOT   |                  |
      | serial: ONE job  |          NAT bridge vmbr1
      | at a time        |          10.20.0.0/24, gw .1
      +-------+----------+                  |
              |                    +--------v---------+
              | iptables           |  guest VMs       |
              | chain NXEON_FWD    |  10.20.0.100-250 |
              | DNAT 20000-29999   |  SSH via DNAT    |
              +------------------->+------------------+
                                            |
                                   +--------v---------+
                                   | Mailcow (VM 8000)|
                                   | Postfix/Dovecot/ |
                                   | Rspamd/SOGo      |
                                   | ~18 containers   |
                                   | mail DNAT chain  |
                                   | NXEON_MAIL       |
                                   +------------------+
```

**The processes, verified from `systemctl cat`:**

| Unit | Runs | User | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nxeon-web` | `/usr/bin/npm start` in `/opt/nxeon` | `nxeon` | Next.js server. Unprivileged — only `.next` is writable by it |
| `nxeon-worker` | `npx tsx worker/index.ts` | **root** | Manages iptables and calls Proxmox; needs root |
| `nxeon-terminal` | `npx tsx terminal-server/index.ts` | `nxeon` | PTY websocket backend for the in-browser terminal, port 8901 |
| `nxeon-console-proxy` | `node scripts/console-proxy.mjs` | root | Relays browser websockets to the Proxmox VNC port, 8899 |
| `nxeon-firewall` | `scripts/firewall.nft` | root | Host nftables ruleset, oneshot |
| `nxeon-mail-nat` | `scripts/mail-nat.sh` | root | DNATs mail ports to the Mailcow VM via its own `NXEON_MAIL` chain |

Every unit takes `EnvironmentFile=/opt/nxeon/.env`. Staging has a parallel set with the
`nxeon-staging-` prefix.

**Timers:**

| Timer | Schedule (observed) | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `nxeon-backup-db.timer` | daily ~03:15 | `pg_dump` of `nxeon` and `nxeon_staging`, 14-day retention |
| `nxeon-backup-vms.timer` | **weekly**, Sun ~04:30 | `vzdump` of customer VMs, keeps 2 |
| `nxeon-backup-offsite.timer` | daily ~04:20 | Replicates off-site — **inert, no target configured** |
| `nxeon-verify-restore.timer` | daily ~05:30 | Restores the newest dump into a scratch DB to prove it works |
| `nxeon-nightly-scan.timer` | daily ~03:32 | `scripts/nightly-scan.ts` writes proposals to the Improvements board |

A failure in any of those triggers `nxeon-alert@<unit>.service`, which notifies admins.

**Networking rules that matter**

- Guests live on the NAT bridge `vmbr1`, `10.20.0.0/24`, gateway `.1`. IPs are allocated from
  `10.20.0.100–250` by `lib/ipam.ts`.
- SSH reaches a guest through a DNAT port-forward in the iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, public ports
  `20000–29999`. **That chain is rebuilt from the database by `worker/network.ts` — never edit it by
  hand.** Anything you add manually disappears on the next sync.
- A server with a dedicated IPv4 is reconfigured onto the public IP and its `sshPort` is set to
  `null`. Two list pages still render `PUBLIC_IP:sshPort` and therefore show `—` for those servers
  (`app/dashboard/page.tsx:174`, `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx:32`); the detail page gets it right.
- Cloud-init is delivered from a vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml`, plus a
  per-server `cicustom` snippet built by `buildCloudInit` (`worker/index.ts:92`).

---

## Request lifecycle — what happens when a customer clicks

Nxeon is almost entirely **server components plus server actions**. There is very little client
state, and no REST layer between the UI and the database for first-party flows. Understanding this
one diagram explains most of the codebase's shape.

```
  browser                     nxeon-web (Next.js)                    Postgres / Proxmox
  -------                     -------------------                    ------------------

  GET /dashboard/servers/x
        |
        |-------------------> app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx
        |                       (server component, force-dynamic)
        |                       currentUser()  <- signed cookie
        |                       db.server.findFirst({ where:{ id, userId }})   ---> SELECT
        |                       lib/proxmox read-only status/RRD              ---> GET /nodes/..
        |<------------------- streamed HTML
        |
  click "Reboot"
        |
        |--- POST (server action, Origin-checked by Next) ------->
        |                     lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts
        |                       1. currentUser()
        |                       2. ownedServer(id, user)      <- the IDOR guard
        |                       3. assertNotImpersonating()   <- money/destructive paths
        |                       4. one-in-flight-job check
        |                       5. db.job.create({ type:"REBOOT" })            ---> INSERT
        |                       6. revalidatePath()
        |<-------------------  { ok:true }
        |
        |   (page re-renders; job is still QUEUED)
        |
        v
                          ...meanwhile, in the worker (next section)
```

**The five guards every mutating action applies.** If you are writing a new action, copy an existing
one — the pattern is consistent and the audits confirmed it holds across all 20+ mutating actions and
all 35 API routes:

1. `currentUser()` / `realUser()` from `lib/auth.ts` — signed cookie, `sessionVersion` checked so a
   password change invalidates old sessions.
2. An `owned*` helper — `ownedServer`, `ownedVolume`, `ownedWebsite`, `ownedDatabase`, `ownedApp`,
   `ownedCron`, `ownedDomain`, `ownedCertificate`, `ownedTargetServer`. These are the reason no IDOR
   was found in two independent passes.
3. `assertNotImpersonating()` on anything that spends money — an admin acting as a customer must not
   be able to charge them. Coverage is **partial**: 6–7 of the money-moving actions have it, not all.
4. The **one in-flight job per server** rule.
5. `revalidatePath()` so the server component re-reads.

**Auth specifics** (`lib/auth.ts`, `lib/actions.ts:150-173`): password hashing is bcrypt; the session
is a `jose`-signed JWT in a cookie named by `NXEON_COOKIE_NAME` (so prod and staging cookies never
collide); login is throttled to 10 attempts per 15 minutes per email+IP and challenges TOTP when
enabled. `impersonateUser()` sets a second signed cookie — `currentUser()` then returns the target
and `realUser()` the actual admin; admin pages call `realUser`/`requireArea` and refuse to render
while impersonating.

**Where API routes are used instead**, and why: `app/api/**` exists for things a server action cannot
do — streaming/binary responses (`/api/invoices/[id]` HTML, `/api/files/[serverId]` up/downloads,
`/api/mail/attachment`, `/api/mail/signature-image/[id]`), third-party callbacks
(`/api/stripe/webhook`, `/api/integrations/cloudflare/callback`), websocket handshakes
(`/api/console/[serverId]`, `/api/terminal/token`), the public token API (`/api/v1/servers`), and
polled reads (`/api/metrics`, `/api/health`, `/api/search`).

---

## Job lifecycle — how work reaches a VM

The worker is a **single-threaded, strictly serial queue**. One job runs platform-wide at a time.
This is the most important operational fact in the document: it makes the system easy to reason about
and it is also the platform's biggest availability weakness.

```
   ACTION                          WORKER (worker/index.ts)
   ------                          ------------------------

  db.job.create                    main() at :1029
   status=QUEUED                     |
   payload={...}                     +--> reapStuckJobs()  :1008
   serverId=...                      |      any RUNNING row from a previous
        |                            |      process -> QUEUED (if attempts<3)
        |                            |      else FAILED + reconcile
        |                            |
        |                            +--> for(;;)  :1041
        |                                   |
        |                                   |  sweeps, by elapsed time:
        |                                   |    10 min  billingSweep + productRenewalSweep
        |                                   |    15 min  scheduledBackupSweep
        |                                   |    10 min  monitorSweep + abuseSweep + disk samples
        |                                   |    90 s    geoEnrichSweep
        |                                   |     5 min  OVH dedicated-IP pool sync
        |                                   |     6 h    gameUpdateSweep
        |                                   |
        |                                   +--> findFirst({ status:QUEUED }) ORDER BY createdAt
        |                                   |      nothing? sleep POLL_MS = 3000ms
        |                                   |
        |                                   +--> ATOMIC CLAIM  :1145
        |                                   |    updateMany where id=? AND status=QUEUED
        |                                   |      -> status=RUNNING, attempts+1
        |                                   |    count===0 means another worker won: skip
        |                                   |
        |                                   +--> runJob()  :938
        |                                          handlers[job.type](job)   :943
        |                                            |
        |                                            +-- Proxmox API / SSH into the guest
        |                                            +-- reportJobProgress(id, pct, step)  :701
        |                                            |
        |                                       success -> status=DONE
        |                                            |
        |                                       throw --> redact root password from the
        |                                                 message  :952-963
        |                                                 attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS(3)?
        |                                                   yes -> back to QUEUED (no backoff!)
        |                                                   no  -> FAILED
        |                                                          reconcileFailedJob()  :891
        |                                                          if type in
        |                                                          VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS
        |                                                            -> Server.status=ERROR
        v
```

**Job types and handlers.** The dispatch table is `handlers` at `worker/index.ts:771`. There is no
`switch` — it is a plain `Record<string, (job)=>Promise<void>>`, so adding a type means adding a
`JobType` enum value in `prisma/schema.prisma:35-71` and a key here. 34 types today:

| Job type | Handler | Lives in |
|---|---|---|
| `PROVISION` | `provision` | `worker/index.ts:193` |
| `START` / `STOP` / `REBOOT` | `powerAction` | `worker/index.ts:331` |
| `DELETE` | `remove` | `worker/index.ts:364` |
| `REINSTALL` | `reinstall` | `worker/index.ts:404` |
| `SUSPEND` / `UNSUSPEND` | `suspend` | `worker/index.ts:460` |
| `RESIZE` | `resize` | `worker/index.ts:555` |
| `SNAPSHOT_CREATE` / `_DELETE` / `_ROLLBACK` | `snapshotOp` | `worker/index.ts:612` |
| `BACKUP_CREATE` | `backupCreate` | `worker/index.ts:724` |
| `BACKUP_RESTORE` | `backupRestore` | `worker/restore.ts` |
| `PASSWORD_RESET` | `passwordReset` | `worker/index.ts:648` |
| `SYNC_FORWARDS` | inline → `syncPortForwards` | `worker/network.ts` |
| `DISK_EXPAND` | `diskExpand` | `worker/disk-expand.ts` |
| `VOLUME_CREATE` / `_ATTACH` / `_DETACH` / `_DELETE` | `volume*` | `worker/volumes.ts` |
| `MIGRATE` | `runMigration` | `worker/migrate.ts` |
| `SSL_ISSUE` | `sslIssue` | `worker/ssl.ts` |
| `GAME_CONFIG` | `gameConfigApply` | `worker/game-config.ts` |
| `GAME_UPDATE` | `gameUpdate` | `worker/game-update.ts` |
| `CLAUDE_BUILD` | `claudeBuild` | `worker/claude.ts` |
| `WEBSITE_CREATE` / `_DELETE` / `_TOGGLE` / `_SSL` | `website*` | `worker/websites.ts` |
| `DB_CREATE` / `DB_DELETE` | `db*` | `worker/databases.ts` |
| `APP_INSTALL` | `appInstall` | `worker/apps.ts` |
| `CRON_SYNC` | `cronSync` | `worker/services.ts` |
| `SERVICE_ACTION` | `serviceAction` | `worker/services.ts` |

**`VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS`** (`worker/index.ts:49`) is the set whose failure means the VM's run or
disk state is genuinely suspect, and therefore flips `Server.status` to `ERROR`. Everything else — a
failed backup, a failed website create, a failed SSL issue — reports through its own notification and
**leaves the server alone**. This exists because a failed backup used to make a running server look
like it had shut down. `BACKUP_CREATE` is deliberately excluded; `BACKUP_RESTORE` is deliberately
included, because a restore has already stopped the VM and begun overwriting its disk.

**Money reconciliation on terminal failure.** Actions charge the wallet *before* enqueuing, so the UI
reflects the change immediately. If the job then fails terminally, `reconcileFailedJob`
(`worker/index.ts:891`) unwinds it: a failed upgrade is refunded, a failed downgrade's credit is
clawed back, and `reconcileFailedDiskExpand` (`:822`) refunds a paid disk expansion — but only when
`Server.extraDiskGB` never reached the job's target, so a partial success (disk grown, filesystem
left for the customer) correctly keeps the charge. Both are idempotent through an `AuditLog` marker.

**What is wrong with this design, stated plainly:**

- **One hung job wedges the platform.** A `MIGRATE` can run 25 minutes; a `BACKUP_RESTORE` has a
  one-hour timeout and retries twice, so a bad restore can stall every other customer's provisioning
  for three hours. There is no per-type concurrency and no queue-position or ETA anywhere in the UI.
  A customer's SSL certificate genuinely sat `PENDING` for 13 minutes behind a migration.
- **No retry backoff.** A failed job goes straight back to `QUEUED` and is re-claimed on the next
  3-second poll, so three attempts can burn in under ten seconds.
- **The one-in-flight-job check is check-then-act.** `applyResize` (`lib/resize.ts:100-131`),
  `applyDiskExpand` (`lib/disk-expand.ts:155-202`) and `queueJob` (`lib/actions-server.ts:31-36`)
  count pending jobs *outside* the transaction that debits and enqueues, so two tabs can both see
  zero and both charge. `orderVolume` (`lib/actions-volumes.ts:55-110`) has no guard at all. The
  right tool already exists — `beginSubmit()` in `lib/actions-domains.ts:42-53` — but it is private
  to that file.

---

## Environments — production, staging and the sandbox flag

Two complete instances on the same host, sharing the Proxmox node but never overlapping. **The code
is identical; every difference is driven by `.env`.**

| | Production | Staging |
|---|---|---|
| Path | `/opt/nxeon` | `/opt/nxeon-staging` |
| Database | `nxeon` | `nxeon_staging` |
| Services | `nxeon-web` (:3000), `nxeon-worker` | `nxeon-staging-web` (:3001), `nxeon-staging-worker` |
| Terminal WS | `nxeon-terminal` (:8901) | `nxeon-terminal-staging` (:8902) |
| Public URL | `https://nxeon.cloud` | `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`, also `:8080` |
| Guest IP pool | `10.20.0.100–250` | `10.20.0.50–99` |
| SSH port pool | `20000–29999` | `30000–30999` |
| iptables chain | `NXEON_FWD` | `NXEON_FWD_STG` |
| Proxmox VM tag | *(none)* | `nxeon-staging` |
| Cookie | `nxeon_session` | `nxeon_session_stg` |
| `NXEON_SANDBOX` | unset | **`1`** |
| Credentials file | `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt` | `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt` |

**`NXEON_SANDBOX=1` is what makes staging safe to break.** With it set (`lib/sandbox.ts`), the worker
**simulates every job**: no Proxmox clone, no VM start, synthetic IPs, no OVH calls, no SSH into
anything. Sweeps that touch Proxmox or OVH are neutralised. Wallet top-ups bypass Stripe and credit
instantly, and a persistent SANDBOX banner marks the environment.

Two things sandbox does **not** change, and both surprise people:

- **Billing still runs.** Wallet debits, renewals, grace and suspension all behave normally on play
  money. There is no simulated branch anywhere in a charge path.
- **It is not a substitute for testing provisioning.** Since no VM is created, staging cannot catch a
  cloud-init or Proxmox regression. Those only surface in production.

**Safety rules that are not negotiable:**

- Never touch VMIDs **9000–9999** — those are the OS templates. There is no code guard on this; the
  only `9000` comparison in the repo is a display filter. `destroyVm` and both resize paths take
  `vmid` straight from the database.
- Staging must only ever allocate `.50–.99` and ports `30000–30999`. Pointing staging pools at
  production ranges would let it hand out an IP a live customer is using.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row. Go through a `DELETE` job so the row, the IP, the
  port-forward, the volumes and the billing all unwind together.

---

## Feature flags and integration switches

Four `ENABLE_REAL_*` flags gate code paths that touch a customer's real infrastructure. They exist so
a dangerous engine can ship and be reviewed before it is trusted. **The trap is that three of the
four have a "simulated success" fallback, and a simulated success that reports success to a paying
customer is a lie.** One of them still does this.

Verified against `/opt/nxeon/.env` at the time of writing:

| Flag | Prod value | Effect when unset | Honest when unset? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` | **`1`** | `worker/migrate.ts` runs a simulation | Yes — flag is on |
| `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` | **`1`** | Control-panel jobs return synthetic data | Yes — flag is on |
| `ENABLE_REAL_SSL` | **`1`** | `worker/ssl.ts:330` **throws** outside sandbox | **Yes, now** — see below |
| `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` | *unset* | `worker/game-config.ts:76-96` stamps a marker and notifies "Game settings applied" | **No — this is a live lie** |

**Correction to earlier documentation.** Both audits recorded `ENABLE_REAL_SSL` as unset on
production, with `worker/ssl.ts` writing a fabricated `ACTIVE` certificate and a made-up 90-day
expiry. That is no longer true on two counts: the flag **is now set to `1`**, and the simulated branch
was rewritten to `throw` whenever `!SANDBOX` (`worker/ssl.ts:330-336`) so a missing flag can never
again be mistaken for a certificate. The one fabricated record in the live database
(`studionexis.com`) has been corrected to `FAILED` with an explanatory `lastError` — I confirmed that
row.

**`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` is the remaining instance of the pattern.** With the flag unset,
`gameConfigApply` writes an `_appliedVariant` / `_appliedAt` marker onto `Server.gameConfig` and
notifies the customer *"Game settings applied on `<hostname>` — Minecraft (vanilla) settings were
applied."* The `(sandbox)` qualifier is appended only when `SANDBOX` is true, which it is not in
production. Nothing touches the VM. Fix it the way SSL was fixed — throw outside sandbox — or enable
the flag and test it on a throwaway VM.

**Integration switches** (presence of credentials, not a boolean flag):

| Integration | Env keys | State |
|---|---|---|

**Single source of truth:** `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`. Four values — `BASE_DOMAIN`, `ADMIN_HOST`,

the admin host and the staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It
regenerates the vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certificates, updates `APP_URL` in both `.env` files

## Wallet, checkout and the wallet/card split

**The model.** Every customer has a wallet: `User.balanceCents`, integer cents, with an append-only
ledger in `WalletTransaction`. All purchases debit the wallet. A card is used only to *top the wallet
up to the amount needed for this purchase*, never to pay a merchant directly. That single design
decision is why the money paths are as simple as they are.

**`walletSplit` is the shared function.** `lib/wallet-split.ts:33` — pure, no server-only imports, so
the client wizard and the server action compute byte-identical numbers.

```
  walletSplit({ dueCents, balanceCents, useWallet })

    useWallet false ............ everything on the card
    balance >= due ............. cardCents = 0, no Stripe at all
    partial .................... walletApplied = min(balance, due)
                                 cardCents     = due - walletApplied
    0 < cardCents < 50 ......... Stripe rejects sub-50c charges, so:
      (and balance can't cover)   walletApplied = due - 50
                                  cardCents     = 50
                                  clampedForStripeMin = true
```

Callers — server: `lib/actions.ts:407` (deploy), `lib/actions-server.ts:148` (upgrade),
`lib/actions-disk.ts:85` (disk). Client: `DeployWizard.tsx:179`, `ResizePicker.tsx:78`,
`AddStorage.tsx:79`. Same function on both sides of every one of those pairs.

**Ordering of money movement, which is subtle and correct.** The card is charged only the remainder.
On success the fulfilment path credits that card amount to the wallet and *then* debits the full
charge (`lib/actions.ts:424-430`, `lib/stripe.ts:48-56`). So the wallet is never touched before the
card clears, and the ledger reads as two honest entries rather than one fudged one.

| `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` | Verifies the signature `:15`; on `checkout.session.completed` it **fulfils** `:34`. Errors are swallowed **on purpose** so a non-2xx makes Stripe retry — Stripe's 3-day retry is the backstop `:29-37` |

Order/resize/disk-expand intents ride in `metadata.nxeonOrder`, truncated to 490 characters
(`lib/stripe.ts:41`). SSH keys are stripped to fit (`:26`) and `extraDiskGB` is left `undefined`
rather than `0` purely to save bytes (`order.ts:75-80`). **There is no length assertion**, so a
silent truncation would corrupt the intent.

**Two independent idempotency layers.** Understanding that these answer *different* questions is the
whole point of the P0-3 fix:

| Layer | Key | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Wallet credit | `UNIQUE WalletTransaction.stripeSessionId` — `lib/stripe.ts:205-244` | "Has this session's money been credited?" |
| Fulfilment | `UNIQUE FulfilledSession.stripeSessionId` — `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:45` | "Has this session's *service* been delivered?" |

**The bug this replaced (commit `02a2bc4`, "P0-3").** Fulfilment used to live inline in the confirm
route and was gated on `creditCheckoutSession()`'s boolean return — which is true only for whoever
won the race to insert the wallet credit. The webhook called the same function and threw the result
away. Two live failure modes:

- **Race.** The webhook's insert lands first; the confirm request gets a P2002, sees
  `credited === false`, and quietly redirects to an empty page. $249 charged, $249 credited, no
  server, no error, no notification.
- **Deterministic.** The customer closes the tab before `success_url` resolves, so the confirm route
  never runs at all. Same outcome, 100% reproducible.

Both applied identically to paid upgrades and paid disk expansions: card charged, wallet credited,
`RESIZE` / `DISK_EXPAND` job never queued, nothing reconciled it.

**Now:** one shared `fulfilCheckoutSession` (`lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:65`) called by **both** the
webhook and the confirm route. It deliberately discards the credit function's return value (`:64-70`
— "conflating who won the credit race with has this been fulfilled was the bug"), claims the session
by *inserting* a `FulfilledSession` row, and dispatches on the intent: `order` → `placeOrder` `:80`,
`resize` → `applyResize` `:109`, `diskExpand` → `applyDiskExpand` `:131`, otherwise plain `topup`
`:147`. A failure after claiming is recorded `FAILED` with the reason and the customer is told their
money is safe in their wallet (`:87-99`).

**Failure modes**

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Customer paid, no server, no error | Fulfilment threw after claiming | Find the `FulfilledSession` row by `stripeSessionId`; `detail` holds the reason. The funds ARE in the wallet — have them deploy again |
| Customer paid twice | Not possible via Checkout — both layers are UNIQUE-backed | Check for two distinct `stripeSessionId` values before believing it |
| "Demo top-up" badge on a real account | `AddFunds.tsx:64` falls back to `DemoTopUp` whenever `/api/stripe/checkout` returns anything containing "not configured" — and `topUp` then refuses in production | Fix the Stripe misconfiguration; the fallback is a trap |

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `/admin/billing` and `/admin/invoices` for the ledger;
`/admin/logs` for the audit and email log. For a payment question the authoritative sequence is:
Stripe dashboard session → `WalletTransaction` row with that `stripeSessionId` → `FulfilledSession`
row with that `stripeSessionId` → the `Server`/`Job` named in its `detail`.

> **Not true yet — reconciliation.** Nothing sweeps `FulfilledSession`. A row stuck in `CLAIMED` or
> `FAILED` is invisible unless someone queries it. `rg fulfilledSession` returns hits only inside
> `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`. A 5-minute worker sweep that alerts on any `CLAIMED` row older than a
> few minutes, or any `FAILED` row at all, is the missing piece.

> **Not true yet — coupons on card top-ups.** `components/customer/CouponField.tsx:60-66` renders
> *"Code applied — 20% bonus · Bonus is credited when you add funds"* and writes an `nxeon_coupon`
> cookie. That cookie is read in exactly one place — `lib/actions.ts:527`, inside the **demo**
> gateway, which refuses in production. `app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts` sets no `discounts` and no
> `allow_promotion_codes`, and `creditCheckoutSession` credits `amount_total` verbatim. The customer
> is promised a bonus and silently gets nothing.

> **Not true yet — auto top-up.** `saveAutoRecharge` (`lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts:20`) has one
> caller, `components/customer/AutoRecharge.tsx:16`, and that component has **zero** live call
> sites — its import is commented out at `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:15` and replaced by a
> "Coming soon" card. The three `autoRecharge*` columns are read only by the GDPR export. This is
> the *right* way to handle an unwired feature and is worth copying: the reason is documented in the
> page, and the customer is never promised anything.

## Invoices

**What it does.** Every automatic charge writes a `PAID` invoice **inside the same transaction that
moves the money**, so a lost race or a retry cannot produce a duplicate document. Invoices are HTML,
not PDF.

**Model** — `prisma/schema.prisma:510`. `number Int @unique @default(autoincrement())`, displayed
zero-padded to five digits (`lib/invoices.ts:147`). `lineItems` is JSON:
`[{description, qty, unitCents, amountCents}]`. `refundedCents` tracks partial refunds.

**Construction.** `invoiceCreateData` (`lib/invoices.ts:72`) returns a plain Prisma `data` payload and
touches no database — deliberately, so each charge site can create the invoice inside its own guarded
transaction and inherit that charge's idempotency (`:65-71`). `amountCents` is always derived from
the line items plus tax so the stamped total cannot desync from the lines (`:82-83`).
`createInvoice` (`:104`) is the direct-write variant for admin use.

**The ten automatic charge sites that write a PAID invoice:** `lib/order.ts:212` (VPS order),
`lib/actions.ts:321` and `:652` (game order, manual renew), `lib/resize.ts:126` (upgrade proration),
`lib/disk-expand.ts:176` (disk), `lib/stripe.ts:231` (top-up), `worker/billing.ts:147` (VPS renewal)
and `:561` (domain renewal), `worker/product-renewals.ts:174` and `:352` (email, volume renewals),
`lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts:268` (transfer-in). `OPEN` invoices come only from admin actions
(`lib/actions-billing.ts:39`, `:118`) and are informational — `generateInvoiceForServer` explicitly
does not charge the wallet.

**Screen** — `/dashboard/invoices` and `/dashboard/invoices/[id]`.

|  00013  2026-07-26   Wallet top-up                   $50.00   [ PAID ]   |
|  00012  2026-07-25   Extra storage +40 GB            $48.00   [ PAID ]   |
|  00011  2026-07-01   Starter - 1 mo - web-2           $8.99   [REFUNDED] |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+

  clicking a row -> /dashboard/invoices/00014

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Invoice 00014                                       [ Print / Save PDF ]|

|  Nxeon                                   Invoice 00014                   |
|  nxeon.cloud                             Issued 2026-07-26               |

|  Jane Doe  jane@example.com                                              |
|                                                                          |
|  Description                      Qty   Unit        Amount               |
|  Standard - 12 months               1   $140.29     $140.29              |
|  ---------------------------------------------------------------------   |
|  Subtotal                                           $140.29              |

```

**Code entry points**

| Thing | Location |
|---|---|
| Payload builder | `invoiceCreateData` — `lib/invoices.ts:72` |
| HTML renderer | `renderInvoiceHTML` — `lib/invoices.ts:141` (print CSS `:262`, print button `:270`) |
| API | `app/api/invoices/[id]/route.ts` — owner-or-admin `:25`, `text/html`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` `:36` |
| Customer list / detail | `app/dashboard/invoices/page.tsx` (200 max), `app/dashboard/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:27` |
| Admin | `app/admin/invoices/page.tsx`, `app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx`, `components/admin/InvoiceAdmin.tsx` |
| Admin actions | `lib/actions-billing.ts` (void, mark paid, generate), `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts` (refunds, bulk, balance adjust) |

**There is no PDF library.** No `pdf`, `puppeteer` or `playwright` in `package.json` — confirmed. The
deliberate approach is print-optimised CSS plus a "Print / Save as PDF" button, documented at
`app/api/invoices/[id]/route.ts:8-13`. If someone asks for real PDF attachments, that is new work.

**Failure modes and known defects**

| Symptom | Cause | Where |
|---|---|---|
| An annual server's admin-generated invoice is ~1/13th of what the customer pays | `generateInvoiceForServer` bills one month at list price, ignoring `termMonths`, `extraDiskGB` and the IP surcharge | `lib/actions-billing.ts:26-41` |
| A server named `web-2` never gets a backfilled invoice | `regenerateMissingInvoices` dedupes on `description contains hostname`, so `web` matches `web-2` | `lib/actions-billing.ts:98-105` |
| A REFUNDED invoice silently becomes VOID and drops out of the "Issued · total" stat | `bulkVoidInvoices` includes `REFUNDED` in its `voidable` set and clears `paidAt`; the single-invoice action refuses anything PAID | `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:189` vs `lib/actions-billing.ts:54-67` |
| A BILLING-role staffer clicking **Mark paid** sees a raw `NEXT_REDIRECT` string in red | Page gates on `requireArea("billing")`, the action gates on `requireAdmin()` which `redirect()`s, and the component displays `e.message` | `app/admin/invoices/[id]/page.tsx:23` vs `lib/actions-billing.ts:55` |
| Tax line always $0 | No charge path passes `taxCents` | see the pricing chapter |

> that bind a refund to a specific invoice. The bug being fixed: `refundPayment` took only
> `(userId, amount)` and picked its Stripe target as "most recent top-up, any amount" — so refunding a

## Renewals, dunning, grace and suspension

**What it does.** A 10-minute worker sweep charges the wallet for expiring subscriptions, and — when
that fails — walks the customer down a defined escalation: notify, grace, suspend, warn, delete.
**It is wallet-only.** There is no card auto-charge. Read the *Not true yet* block at the end before
you tell a customer anything about payment retries.

**The sweeps.** `billingSweep()` and `productRenewalSweep()` both run from the worker's main loop
every 10 minutes (`worker/index.ts:1042-1055`).

**Constants** — `worker/billing.ts:27-34`, all env-overridable:

| Constant | Default | Env |
|---|---|---|
| `GRACE_DAYS` | 3 | `NXEON_GRACE_DAYS` |
| `TERMINATE_DAYS` | 10 | — |
| `WARN_BEFORE_TERMINATE_DAYS` | 2 | — |
| `DOMAIN_RENEW_WINDOW_DAYS` | 7 | — |

`RENEW_DAYS = 30` at `:28` is declared and never referenced — dead.

**The VPS state machine.** All offsets are relative to `expiresAt`, called `E`.

```
        E-3d              E              E+3d          E+11d        E+13d
          |               |                |              |            |
  --------+---------------+----------------+--------------+------------+------->
          |               |                |              |            |
   "renews soon,     charge the        SUSPEND         "will be      DELETE
    action needed"   wallet            suspendReason    deleted        VM + data
                                       = UNPAID         soon"         permanently
   ONLY if the       CAS on expiresAt  SUSPEND job                    DELETE job
   renewal WOULD     -> debitWallet    audit + notify   deduped 2d
   fail (autoRenew   -> WalletTxn                                     status
   off, or balance   -> PAID Invoice   server keeps                   -> DELETING
   short).           -> AuditLog       running through
   deduped 4d       all in ONE tx      grace (E..E+3d)

  billing.ts:53-88   :124-177          :192-219        :452-471      :431-451
```

**Renewal amount** (`worker/billing.ts:109-116`): undiscounted `vpsTermPriceCents` — the promo was
first-term only — plus the dedicated-IP surcharge **only if a real `DedicatedIp` row exists** (not
merely the `wantsDedicatedIp` intent flag, `:112-115`), plus `extraDiskGB × monthlyRate × months`.
Manual `renewNow` mirrors this exactly (`lib/actions.ts:615-618`).

**Double-charge protection.** Every renewal path does a compare-and-swap on `expiresAt` and throws
`AlreadyRenewedError` if it lost (`worker/billing.ts:25,129-133`; `lib/actions.ts:635-639`). The code
carries an explicit warning that the sweep's snapshot of `balanceCents` is stale by the time the
charge runs and must never gate it (`billing.ts:118-122`) — the atomic conditional `updateMany` inside
`debitWallet` (`lib/wallet.ts:22-26`) is the only thing allowed to decide.

**`Server.suspendReason` — why it exists.** Values `"UNPAID" | "ABUSE" | "ADMIN"`, null meaning never
suspended (`prisma/schema.prisma:329`, documented at `:315-328`).

| Value | Set at | Cleared at |
|---|---|---|
| `UNPAID` | `worker/billing.ts:203` | `lib/actions.ts:637` (successful renewal), `worker/index.ts:464`, `:512` (unsuspend) |
| `ABUSE` | `lib/actions-abuse.ts:42` | as above |
| `ADMIN` | `lib/actions.ts:779` | `lib/actions.ts:780` |

It is consumed in exactly two places, both scoped strictly to `UNPAID`: the `terminateOverdue`
selector (`worker/billing.ts:426`) and `renewNow`'s auto-unsuspend (`lib/actions.ts:690`).

**The bug it was added for (commit `78407bd`, "P0-8").** `suspendedNote` was the only thing
distinguishing an unpaid suspension from an abuse or admin one, and **nothing consumed it**. Two live
consequences:

- **A paid-up customer's server was permanently deleted.** `terminateOverdue` selected on
  `status: "SUSPENDED"` alone, while the renewal sweep *excludes* suspended servers
  (`billing.ts:94` restricts to `RUNNING`/`STOPPED`). So an admin suspending a paid-up customer
  pending an abuse review meant that customer was never charged and never warned; their term lapsed
  untouched, and 13 days later their VM and all its data were destroyed with a "prolonged
  non-payment" notice they had never been given the chance to act on. They had auto-renew on and a
  funded wallet.
- **An abuse suspension could be reversed with a credit card.** `renewNow` auto-unsuspended *any*
  suspended server on payment, so a spammer suspended for outbound abuse could pay and put
  themselves straight back on the network.

Legacy rows with `suspendReason = null` are excluded from **both** paths. The rationale is recorded at
`worker/billing.ts:419-421` and is worth internalising as a general principle: *failing to terminate
costs disk; wrongly terminating is unrecoverable.*

**Add-on product renewals** — `worker/product-renewals.ts`, with the decision logic kept pure in
`lib/product-billing.ts` (`renewalDecision` at `:153` returns `renew | grace | enforce`).
`PRODUCT_GRACE_DAYS` shares `NXEON_GRACE_DAYS`; `PRODUCT_WARN_DAYS = 3`. Enforcement is deliberately
non-destructive:

| Product | On non-payment |
|---|---|
| Business email | Subscription → `SUSPENDED`, mailboxes kept — `product-renewals.ts:209-234` |
| Block-storage volume | → `DETACHED` plus a `VOLUME_DETACH` job, **data kept** — `:385-456`, honouring the in-flight guard `:417-423` |

`PRODUCT_RECLAIM_DAYS` is messaging only — nothing deletes (`lib/product-billing.ts:36-42`).

**How an admin diagnoses a billing question.** `/admin/subscriptions` shows terms and expiry;
`/admin/users/[id]` shows the wallet ledger; `/admin/servers/[id]` shows `suspendReason` and
`suspendedNote`. To answer "why was this suspended", read `suspendReason` first — that single field
tells you whether billing or a human did it.

> **Not true yet — there is no card auto-charge, and this is the largest gap in the product.**
> Verified by grep across the whole repo:
>
> - `Server.dunningStage`, `dunningNextAt` and `dunningPayUrl` (`prisma/schema.prisma:331-346`) are
>   **never read or written by any code**. The columns and their careful comments exist; the engine
>   does not.
> - Zero hits for `off_session`, `paymentIntents.create`, `SetupIntent` or `setup_future_usage`.
>   `User.stripeCustomerId` and `stripePaymentMethodId` are never written and never read; the only
>   mention is a comment in the GDPR export route. `User.cardBrand`/`cardLast4`/`cardExpMonth`/
>   `cardExpYear`/`cardExpiryNotifiedAt` and `WalletTransaction.stripePaymentIntentId` are the same
>   kind of furniture — schema built ahead of an engine that was never written.
> - `lib/mailer.ts:218-236` documents *"Renewals apply wallet credit first, then auto-charge the
>   customer's saved card… we retry on day 1, 3 and 5"* with `DUNNING_RETRY_ATTEMPTS = 3` at `:236`.
>   **None of that exists.**
>
> Actual behaviour: `debitWallet` fails → grace → suspend. **A customer with a perfectly good card is
> suspended when their wallet empties.**

> **Not true yet — no email is sent for any billing event.** `rg sendMail worker/*.ts` returns zero

> **Not true yet — the admin dunning panel is inert.** `dunning_grace_days` (3),
> `dunning_warn_days` (7) and `dunning_terminate_days` (14) are editable in
